author.name: Jannik Aßfalg
credits: repeat98: original 808/909 engines, the 0.2.0 ColdFire rewrite and machine integration

presentation.summary: 808 and 909 bassdrum engines; 909 body and transient fitted more closely to private TR-909 direct-out recordings.
presentation.overview: Analog BD synthesizes 808 and 909 bassdrums in the Octatrack DSP. Version 0.1.6 rearranges SRC SETUP to TYPE, FIXD, ACNT above LOW, HIGH, LPF: TYPE picks 808 or 909 and replaces the engine browser, FIXD ON makes every hit identical (OFF, the default, varies each hit slightly, now on the 808 too), and LPF is OFF fully clockwise. HIGH edits over USB, and a double tap on TRACK opens the machine list.
highlights: TYPE and FIXD switches in SRC SETUP; the engine browser is gone
Restore valid stock SRC defaults when leaving Analog BD
909 harmonic phase/asymmetry and complete-hit envelope/DC fit
Minimum/maximum Attack and final-hit Tune endpoints refined
Existing TDEP/SAT smoothing retained; SETUP reordered and LPF OFF moved to fully clockwise
0.1.5 projects keep their 808/909 choice; set ACNT, LPF and FIXD again
usage: Assign ANALOG BD in the track machine chooser or SRC SETUP. Then use the TYPE switch at the top left of SRC SETUP to choose 808 (left) or 909 (right).

Shape the drum on SRC. The 808 has TONE and SWEP; the 909 has TUNE and TDEP. SRC SETUP holds TYPE, FIXD and ACNT above LOW, HIGH and LPF; LPF fully clockwise is OFF. FIXD ON makes every hit identical. AMP controls track volume.

Switching from Analog BD restores stock SRC playback and SETUP defaults automatically. Select your sample and review existing SRC parameter locks, scenes and LFO destinations, which retain their parameter-slot assignments.

Keep a separate project copy for stock firmware: saving an Analog BD project without this module can clamp its controls. Eight voices do not guarantee enough processing room for every effect combination.

controls.name: PTCH
controls.doc: Body pitch. 909: one octave, 32.7 Hz at 0, the recorded 909 (45.6 Hz) at 64, 65.4 Hz at 127.

controls.name: DCAY
controls.doc: Body decay. 909: 15 ms at 0, the recording (247 ms) at 80, 600 ms at 127; the 808 keeps its own law.

controls.name: ATK
controls.doc: Transient strength: the 808's trigger transient; the 909's click, attack noise and lead-in.

controls.name: SWEP / TDEP
controls.doc: 808 pitch bend; 909 pitch-envelope depth and the thump that comes with it.

controls.name: TYPE
controls.doc: SRC SETUP top left: 808 (left) or 909 (right). Switching keeps the other control bytes; a sounding hit finishes on its model.

controls.name: FIXD
controls.doc: SRC SETUP top middle. OFF varies every hit slightly (909: sweep depth, click strength, lead-in level and noise; 808: trigger transient strength); ON makes every hit open identically.

controls.name: ACNT
controls.doc: Accent, SRC SETUP top right: level and attack. The recordings are ACNT 72; above about 95 a 909 can reach full scale and clips.

limitations: Needs the Modwerk base over USB, in a version with machine rows (ot_machines). Card firmware cannot include it; 0.1.x's card build is gone.
Until its CPU price is measured the base charges each Analog BD track its default share, so a fourth Analog BD track in one Part is refused (CPU FULL).
SAT, LOW, HIGH and LPF (0.1.x's desk) are gone; their bytes stay in saved Parts, unread. Kicks that used them, or ACNT near 127, sound different from 0.1.7.
909 reference: one decay-modified TR-909 at one recorded decay setting; the full modified range and the exact intermediate knob positions are not reproduced.

Tested on one MKII (24 Nov 2026): sound, picks on up to three tracks, retriggers, the cost curve and rollback. Not yet tested: MKI, save/reload and a power cycle with Analog BD tracks, eight tracks with heavy effects.
Saving a project with Analog BD tracks on stock firmware can clamp its controls; keep a copy for stock.

resources.recorded: 24 Nov 2026: package 934c9557 (this code) on the owner's MKII, twin of base 0.8.1

storage.label: Storage
storage.conditions: From the USB package (build.py): 37,592 bytes of ColdFire code and data (about 28 KB of tables: the 909 body in three band-limited copies, click, noise and lead-in, the 808's body and transient) and 2,272 of bss (eight voices). No DSP code or DSP memory, no heap, no stock code written.

processing.label: Frame interrupt
processing.conditions: The longest frame's rise with Analog BD on one, two and three empty tracks of a medium pattern (Dev17 C04: trigs on steps 1/5/9/13 of six tracks, two playing samples, 77.9 % stock alone), picked on an empty one; 0.1.7 on the same scene added 20.7/32.6/40.8 and a DSP voice each. No render dropped, no stall. Installed on no track it adds nothing.

impact.conditions: Per Analog BD track; the 909's attack (first 50 ms) is its busiest stretch, a resting voice costs nothing.

cpu.rationale: Each Analog BD track renders on the ColdFire in the frame interrupt. On the owner's MKII the first track added 8.7 % of the longest frame and each further one about 4 %, against 0.1.7's 20.7 % and 8 to 12 % (which also held a DSP voice each).

dsp.rationale: No DSP code and no change to the DSP programs: the samples go to the packer as a sample's do, and the track's own AMP and effects run as stock. 0.1.x's DSP voice and its DSP memory are gone.

memory.rationale: 39,864 bytes in the module pool (37,592 of code and tables, 2,272 of voice state), from the package; no DSP memory, no heap.

tests.summary: 0.2.0: rewritten as a ColdFire machine (no DSP). The 909 keeps 0.1.7's fit and adds the lead-in every recorded hit shows; the 808 matches 0.1.7's at -50 to -55 dB. On the owner's MKII (24 Nov 2026): played over USB in four trials (sound bugs he heard fixed in between: aliasing, block-rate whine, retrigger clicks, stale knob values), the final build approved by ear; cost curve first 8.7 / each 4.0 % of the longest frame (0.1.7: 24.4 / 8.2 and a DSP voice), at rest 0, no render dropped. Not tested: MKI, project save/reload and power cycle with Analog BD tracks.

tutorial.title: Compare the 909 direct-out response
steps: In a disposable project, hold FUNC and press SRC for SRC SETUP, choose ANALOG BD and press YES. Turn the top-left TYPE switch to the right for the 909. Set LOW/HIGH to 64 and SAT to 0.

For the direct-out reference, set PTCH 64, DCAY 80, TUNE 0, TDEP 64, ACNT 72 and LPF 127 (OFF). Trigger repeated hits at 70 BPM and sweep ATK alone through 0–127, then hold it at one value to hear the small strength/noise differences.

Hold ATK at 0 and sweep TUNE through its endpoints separately. Return SAT to 0 and TDEP to 64, then press STOP and let the tail finish. Turn TYPE to the left to compare the 808; its saved knob values remain intact.

access.location: Audio track SRC SETUP: ANALOG BD; its TYPE switch (808 / 909) is the top-left control.
steps: Select an audio track with its TRACK key.
Hold FUNC and press SRC to open SRC SETUP. Use DOWN to reach ANALOG BD, then press YES to assign it.
Press SRC to close SETUP and edit the main controls. The 808 model uses PTCH, DCAY, TONE, ATK, SWEP and SAT; the 909 uses TUNE and TDEP in place of TONE and SWEP.

In SRC SETUP, turn the top-left TYPE switch left for the 808 or right for the 909. Selecting a model retains the existing knob settings. FIXD (top middle) ON makes every hit identical; LPF (bottom right) is OFF fully clockwise.
Hold FUNC and press SRC for the shared ACNT, LPF, LOW and HIGH controls. AMP and the track FX pages remain available.
